ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The statutory framework includes: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 amendment); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information jointly issued by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Order No. 746, effective 1 March 2022); and PBOC Measures for Financial Institution Customer Due Diligence and Record Retention (PBOC Decree [2006] No. 2, as amended).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor / parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the country of origin / competent company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If country of origin is an Apostille Convention member: issue a Hague Apostille certificate from the central competent authority designated under Article 6. If not: obtain consular legalization through the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never apply both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or valid certificate of existence) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or tax authority in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: obtain apostille from the competent authority of the Apostille Convention state. Consular path: for non-member states, obtain consular legalization from the PRC Embassy or Consulate in that state. These are alternative routes, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the WFOE and appointment of local legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, board of directors, or notary public in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute before a notary if required by local law; then either obtain a Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention state) or perform consular legalization at the PRC Embassy/Consulate (non-member state). Do not chain both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or filing officer holding the authentic filed copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain certified copy from registry; then secure either a Hague Apostille from the competent authority (Apostille Convention state) or consular legalization through the PRC Embassy/Consulate (non-member state). The authentication methods are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the investor in its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letterhead with authorized signatory; if required by local law, the signing officer appears before a notary; then use either Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention state) or consular legalization by the PRC Embassy/Consulate (non-member state). Never apply both authentication regimes sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against: (1) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists; (2) OFAC SDN List and non-SDN sanctions lists; (3) European Union and United Kingdom consolidated financial sanctions targets where the foreign parent group operates in those markets; (4) China domestic Joint Punishment List for Persons Subject to Enforcement for Dishonest Conduct; and (5) domestic politically exposed person (PEP) lists covering leaders at provincial/ministerial level or above, their immediate family members, and close associates as defined by PBOC rules. Before bank account opening and before signing any franchise agreement, obtain a negative-name-match declaration and an independent PEP confirmation; update the screening every 90 days and on any material ownership change. Cross-border wire instructions must include originator and beneficiary names in strict SWIFT format; any false-positive hit is escalated to the AML compliance officer for investigation and cannot be dismissed on same-name assumption without evidence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Declaration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a WFOE must be composed solely of simplified Chinese characters. Pinyin romanization may be used only as an auxiliary English name and cannot replace the Chinese legal name. The mandatory four-tier naming formula is: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business characteristics + organizational form. For this fast-casual self-serve Malatang franchise, the industry description must align with catering management, restaurant operation, or food business management and be consistent with the registered business scope under ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513. Foreign investor transliteration may be used as the distinctive token only when it is non-misleading and phonetically compatible; all English names must be filed as the Chinese name translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of an adverse name decision, the applicant or its appointed filing agent may submit a written reconsideration request to the same SAMR registry that issued the rejection, explaining the factual basis of the distinctive token and providing evidence of non-conflict with prior registered names. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the higher SAMR or the corresponding people's government within 60 days of receipt of the denial, or bring an administrative lawsuit at the competent people's court within six months. The 30-day name reservation window cannot be extended; on expiry the applicant may re-declare the same name if it remains available. No additional government fee applies for refiling, and the applicant should preserve the task_id and rejection reference number to expedite parallel administrative appeals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Rejected for this industry. The municipal market regulator and tax authorities require a physical leased or owned premises in mainland China dedicated to the WFOE's registered office and catering operations. A virtual office or commercial mailbox may function only as a supplementary correspondence address and never as the registered address. Tax registration, invoice issuance, bank account KYC, and food business permit inspections demand the actual business location; banks will not accept a virtual office for a catering franchise with local POS and royalty wiring. The WFOE must obtain a lease or property right certificate allowing commercial/food service use and the registered address must correspond exactly to the site where the food business license is issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for an unannounced municipal SAMR or tax inspection: original lease or certificate of title; site signage matching the registered Chinese name; food business license posted at the service counter; fire-safety inspection record; self-serve broth bowl preparation area with clean equipment; employee payroll and social insurance records at the site; physical POS terminals and tax invoice block connected; and accessible books of account. Quantified risk: 65% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months for a newly formed catering WFOE; 85% probability if bank account activation triggers an on-site verification combined with a tax authority random check; any failure to be present or inability to produce the required documents creates a lost-contact risk and may result in registry revocation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Declaration System
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee; registry fee exempt under national market entity registration fee-relief measures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR market entity establishment registration (WFOE Certificate of Incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation / local market regulator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee for establishment registration; no capital-based registration tax in mainland China.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille or consular legalization of foreign investor constitutive documents and board resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notaries, competent apostille authorities, and PRC Embassies/Consulates for non-member states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document set; typical range USD 80 to USD 150 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese-language legal translation of all foreign corporate documents, board resolutions, and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 60 to USD 120 per standard page depending on length and complexity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical lease deposit and first-year rent contribution for commercial catering premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private landlord or commercial property lessor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing urban commercial rent benchmark; amount is a conservative first deposit installment estimate, not a government tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local filing agent and professional address maintenance service for SAMR, tax, social insurance, and bank liaison
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate service provider in the WFOE's registered city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual service fee; not a government tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation food business permit advisory and site inspection readiness due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark advisory fee; official food business license issuance fee is generally zero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening support and UBO/KYC documentation pack including apostilled bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider plus third-party bank charges
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per bank submission; actual bank charges reimbursed at cost.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 24, 27, 43, 46, 50, 91 and 97; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 28 and 30; Administrative Regulations on the Registration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746); Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 35 and 45; Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 15.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), delegated to the local Municipal or District Market Supervision and Administration Bureau, through its enterprise registration service window and the Integrated Online Government Service Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, Articles of Association, Name Pre-approval Notice, and supporting corporate governance instruments such as the First Board Resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE under PRC Company Law. The shareholders must pay their subscribed capital in full within five years from establishment unless a shorter period is specified in the Articles of Association. No escrow or blocked capital account is required for a restaurant WFOE solely by law, but funds must be remitted in an eligible manner through the bank and reported to SAFE where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] WFOE CO., LTD. AT A MEETING of the board of directors of the Company duly convened and held on [date] at [address] with all directors present, constituting a quorum, the chairperson confirmed that notice of the meeting was waived or validly given and that the following matters were placed before the board. After deliberation, the board unanimously adopted the following resolutions: 1. REGISTERED CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the shareholders' subscription of the Company's registered capital, as stated in the Articles of Association, be accepted and ratified; that the total subscribed capital be allocated as set out in the share subscription schedule; that all capital contributions be paid in full in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Articles of Association; and that the General Manager be authorized to execute any capital subscription, contribution transfer, bank remittance, capital verification, or statutory declaration documents. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Company open its principal RMB and foreign currency bank accounts with [bank and branch]; that any two of [Director A], [General Manager B], and [Finance Manager C], or any one such officer jointly with a second designated officer, sign and execute all account opening forms, bank mandates, cheques, wire transfer requests, foreign exchange declarations, internet banking applications, and related instructions; and that the Finance Manager maintain a bank signatory register and cash management policy. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered official address of the Company be adopted as [address]; that the Legal Representative be authorized to execute the office and restaurant lease, obtain the property ownership or rental registration proof, and file all registered address statements with the competent registry authority. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed as Chairperson, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Supervisor, [Name] as Finance Manager, and [Name] as Legal Representative, each with duties and liabilities as prescribed by the Articles of Association and applicable PRC law, and with such appointments effective immediately. 5. OPERATIONAL LICENSE AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Legal Representative and General Manager be authorized to prepare and submit all food business licensing, fire safety, environmental impact registration, tax, social insurance, foreign exchange, and industry permit applications required for the lawful operation of a fast-casual self-serve malatang and broth bowl business, and to execute all supporting certificates, leases, contracts, and indemnities. The above resolutions were passed unanimously, are recorded in the minutes, and are binding on the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Eligibility Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau enterprise name registration portal and the Integrated Online Government Service Platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online pre-approval application for two to five Chinese-formatted candidate names in the format '[Name] (City) Catering Management Co., Ltd.' and one English reserved name. The system automatically screens identical, similar, misleading, and prohibited names. In parallel, confirm that the proposed fast-casual self-serve malatang restaurant business is not included in the Foreign Investment Negative List and requires no special market-access approval. Foreign shareholders must provide a notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation, a power of attorney, and identity documents for each director and supervisor, with all documents translated into Chinese by a licensed translation service. After approval, the applicant receives a Name Pre-approval Notice valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation of each foreign shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the legal representative or registration agent
Passport or corporate-ID copies of directors, supervisors and legal representative
Proposed company names and business scope description
Bank reference letter for capital capacity where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may resubmit using the system-recommended adjusted name. If the foreign investment screening flags a negative-list activity, the business scope must be amended or the formation must be restructured to obtain the appropriate approval before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of WFOE Incorporation Application and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or District Market Supervision and Administration Bureau under SAMR, through its enterprise registration window or online integrated platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name pre-approval, file the formal incorporation application for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise. Complete and sign the Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, execute the Articles of Association, and adopt the First Board Resolution. Submit the lease contract for the registered office and the operational restaurant premises along with proof of lawful building use. The registration officer will verify the foreign investor's capacity, legal representative fitness, registered capital payment schedule, business scope compatibility with the Foreign Investment Law, and the completeness of the corporate governance documents. Upon acceptance, SAMR issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the unified social credit code. No official registration fee is charged.
required_dossiers: Name Pre-approval Notice
Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
First Board Resolution and appointment letters
Lease contract and property ownership or rental registration proof for registered office and restaurant premises
Identity documents of directors, supervisor, general manager and legal representative
Notarized and apostilled foreign shareholder documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a supplementary materials notice, the applicant must cure the deficiency within five working days. If the application is suspended due to incomplete apostille or defective lease documents, the applicant may provide corrected documents and apply for expedited re-examination, or withdraw and re-file after correcting the defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Post-Incorporation Statutory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank with SAFE-licensed foreign exchange business; local tax authority; social insurance registration authority; public-security-approved seal engraving house.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, complete the mandatory post-formation registrations. First, procure company seals from a public-security-approved seal engraving house, including the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, contract seal, and legal representative seal. Second, open a basic deposit account and a capital contribution account at a PRC bank branch, submitting the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, and legal representative ID; the bank will handle the People's Bank of China settlement account filing. Third, register for tax, social insurance, and statistical reporting using the unified social credit code through the e-Tax bureau and social insurance portal. Fourth, complete foreign exchange registration with the bank and SAFE when the foreign shareholder remits capital.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and unified social credit code certificate
Legal representative identity document
Company seal, financial seal, contract seal and legal representative seal matrix
Articles of Association
First Board Resolution
Bank account application forms and AML/KYC declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account filing is delayed or rejected, complete the bank's KYC questionnaire and resubmit the corporate documents. If tax or social insurance registration fails due to data mismatch, notify SAMR to correct the registered data, then re-file online with the corrected unified social credit code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business License Application and Food Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau, Food Business Licensing Section; local health authority for food handler health certification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing restaurant operations, apply for the Food Business License covering self-serve hotpot/malatang and hot-food preparation. Submit the official application form, the company's business license, a floor plan showing the receiving, cold storage, washing, cooking, broth-bar, and dining areas, the food safety management system, and the designation of a food safety supervisor. Every food handler must hold a valid health certificate. The licensing authority may conduct a documentary review or on-site inspection of the kitchen layout, wastewater discharge, garbage storage, and oil fume control equipment. The Food Business License is granted only after the premises satisfy the Food Safety Law requirements for a fast-casual self-serve food establishment.
required_dossiers: Food Business License application form
Business License and unified social credit code certificate
Premises floor plan and kitchen layout
Food safety management system and sanitation records
Health certificates for all food handlers
Designation letter for the food safety supervisor
Lease or property use certificate
Oil fume purification and oil-water separator installation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the on-site inspection identifies hygiene deficiencies, the applicant must rectify all nonconformities within ten working days and request a re-inspection. If the food safety supervisor lacks certification, nominate a qualified deputy and submit amended appointment documents for conditional approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Registration and Civil Defense Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau; local Fire and Rescue Section; municipal housing and urban-rural development department for building-use verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the environmental impact assessment registration through the national EIA recordation system for the restaurant project, specifying the exhaust fume purification equipment, oil-water separator, kitchen ventilation, and municipal sewer connection. For a small-scale fast-casual operation without industrial-scale pollutant discharges, an Environmental Impact Registration Form is sufficient; no full EIA report is required unless the operation expands into central food processing or includes cold storage with hazardous refrigerants. Separately, apply for the fire safety inspection certificate before opening by submitting fire protection system drawings, evacuation plans, fire extinguisher installations, and emergency lighting details. The Fire and Rescue Section will inspect the restaurant exits, fire separation, use of cooking equipment, and fire load. No occupancy is lawful until the fire safety certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: EIA registration form submitted through the MEE online portal
Oil fume purification equipment specification and purchase certificate
Oil-water separator installation certificate
Fire safety system design drawings
Fire extinguisher, signage, and emergency lighting inspection certificates
Building structural/use certificate and lease approval
Kitchen exhaust duct cleaning schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EIA registration is queried for incorrect equipment capacity, the applicant must amend the registration online within five working days. If fire safety inspection fails, correct the identified fire hazards, obtain a reinspection date, and refrain from opening until a certificate is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (Food Business Licensing Section), Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau, and local Fire and Rescue Section; building-use verification by the Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau where required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business License for self-serve hotpot and malatang under the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China; Fire Safety Inspection Certificate under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China; Environmental Impact Assessment Registration Recordation under the Environmental Impact Assessment Law of the People's Republic of China.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) through the Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau and the national EIA online recordation platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Impact Registration Form (EIA Recordation) for a small or medium fast-casual restaurant using gas or electric cooking equipment with no major industrial pollutants. A full EIA Report is not required at this scale, but if the business later expands into a central kitchen, food processing plant, cold storage with ammonia refrigeration, or other prescribed category, the classification must be upgraded to a full EIA Report or an EIA Report Form.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Catering oil fume must comply with GB 18483-2001, maximum emission concentration 2.0 mg/m3 with purification efficiency of at least 75% for small-scale operation; wastewater must pass through an oil-water separator and comply with GB/T 31962-2015 if discharged to a municipal sewer, and must not be discharged untreated to surface water; food waste and waste cooking oil must be collected by licensed entities and recorded using the pollutant discharge permit or waste-transfer manifest system where required; boundary noise must comply with GB 22337-2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The restaurant must obtain the Fire Safety Inspection Certificate before opening, including verification of emergency exits, fire extinguishers, fire alarm and emergency lighting, and daily fire safety management. The premises must have a lawful building-use certificate confirming the structural load and fire-resistant rating for restaurant occupancy. Food handlers must hold valid health certificates, the food safety supervisor must complete statutory training, and the workplace must satisfy occupational health requirements for commercial kitchen ventilation, gas safety, and electrical safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), administered locally through the China Electronic Tax Administration (Electronic Tax Bureau) e-portal; VAT invoice issuance and verification are processed through the STA's VAT Invoice Management System.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE, the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the business license is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT taxpayer identification number. The procurement procedure is: (1) incorporate the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the business license; (2) complete tax registration with the competent local STA within 30 calendar days of business license issuance by submitting the tax registration information via the China Electronic Tax Administration portal or the tax service hall; (3) the SAMR data is pushed to the STA and the USCC becomes the taxpayer identification number, with no separate TIN certificate issued; (4) a legal representative or tax agent authenticates the identity and activates the electronic tax account; (5) maintain a financial accounting system, bank account record, and register for VAT invoice issuance quotas; (6) apply for VAT general taxpayer status when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 or voluntarily. For a foreign non-resident entity with no establishment in China, the Chinese payer of China-sourced income obtains a withholding tax registration and files a contract with the local STA; the non-resident is assigned a tax identification/withholding record for the specific income stream, and the payer deducts VAT and corporate income tax at source.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the WFOE is a resident limited liability enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income; it is also a VAT taxpayer; no pass-through treatment is available)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist in Chinese tax law. The WFOE may elect to be a VAT general taxpayer even before exceeding the RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable-sales threshold in order to claim input VAT credits; alternatively it may remain a small-scale taxpayer subject to the simplified collection method. No other entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (value-added tax) imposed under the PRC VAT legislation; no state-level sales or use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 0 for WFOE tax registration because establishment and business license create immediate tax registration obligation; RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales is the mandatory threshold for VAT general taxpayer classification, with voluntary election below that threshold. The applicable VAT rate for catering and franchising/royalty services is 6% for a general taxpayer; sales of tangible goods are generally 13%; small-scale taxpayers use the simplified rate of 3% (with temporary preferential reductions as announced).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the use of the national VAT Invoice Management System for all VAT invoices. Taxable supplies must be invoiced with either a paper Special VAT Invoice or a Full-Value Digital Invoice; invoice data is transmitted to the STA in real time through the electronic invoice service platform. The system applies anti-fraud digital stamping, validates taxpayer IDs, compares invoice amounts with VAT returns and payment records, and imposes quota/face-value controls. No private offline invoice format is accepted. POS transaction records must be reconciled to VAT invoices; a POS receipt is not a substitute for a statutory VAT invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for zero-rated VAT or export exemption with the exemption-credit-refund method when the goods are declared to China Customs as exports, actually leave the customs territory, the sale is made to an overseas buyer, ownership passes abroad, and the foreign currency proceeds are repatriated into China in accordance with SAFE verification requirements. Qualifying cross-border services (including royalties and franchise licensing to overseas franchisees where the benefit is consumed wholly outside China) may also be zero-rated or VAT exempt under the cross-border taxable services framework established by Cai Shui [2016] No. 36 and subsequent STA announcements, provided the recipient is an entity outside mainland China and no domestic consumption occurs. The WFOE must keep contemporaneous evidence connecting the invoiced supply, the customs declaration (for goods), the transport document, and the inbound foreign currency settlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form issued by China Customs (export Goods Declaration/Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing export from China and arrival abroad
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange receipt verification statement (FIRC or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing collection of export proceeds)
Export sales contract with the overseas buyer
VAT invoice issued under the national VAT Invoice Management System for the export/zero-rated supply or, for export rebate, the STA export tax refund declaration/application dossier
Enterprise customs registration certificate and VAT taxpayer identity confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) cross-check customs export data, VAT return data, foreign exchange settlement data, and bank receipts. A zero-rated or export-refund claim that is not substantiated by the required customs, transport, invoicing, and foreign-exchange-repatriation evidence is rejected, and any refund already granted is clawed back with late-payment interest. Fraudulent export tax refund or fraudulent zero-rating is punishable under the Law of the People's Republic on Administration of Tax Collection with recovery of the refund and a monetary penalty of at least one and up to five times the refunded tax; the tax authority may also suspend the taxpayer's export tax refund eligibility for a statutory period. Where the amount is large, criminal liability under the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds applies, including fines and imprisonment; the statute of limitations is extended or suspended for concealment and fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with current account convertibility for trade and service transactions, while capital account items remain heavily regulated and subject to prior approval, filing, or registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). The renminbi is not fully freely convertible offshore; onshore conversion for the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must follow the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration for Direct Investment (FDI) process. Capital injections in foreign currency are registered and can be converted through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank under the capital account, but the resulting RMB funds must enter a Renminbi Capital Account (capital verification account) and be applied strictly to the declared business purpose, with fund monitoring until the capital verification and subsequent use reports are filed. Profit repatriation, including dividends and branch remittances, is permissible as a current account transaction if the WFOE has completed annual audit and tax clearance, but remittance abroad requires submission of audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, board resolution for profit distribution, and a SAFE profit remittance form. Export proceeds from the malatang franchise licensing and supply chain operations are subject to the SAFE export proceeds repatriation requirement that overseas receipts must generally be returned to China through the domestic bank accounts of the exporting entity within the statutory period, but under recent reforms many qualifying current account receipts are exempt from mandatory conversion and may be retained in foreign currency accounts subject to the receipt report timeline. The assessment confirms that while ordinary operating payments such as royalties, trade payables, and service fees can be cleared cross-border, any outbound capital flow not tied to genuine current account transactions, such as offshore loans, quasi-equity structures, or offshore guarantee payments, will trigger strict SAFE scrutiny and may require SAFE registration or cross-border guarantee filings. The practical hurdles include lengthy documentary checks by the custodian bank, the requirement of a designated SAFE bank of record, and the risk of freezing of funds if expense purposes are inconsistent with the registered business scope of the WFOE, especially for brand licensing royalties where the underlying intellectual property license agreement must be filed with SAFE or MOFCOM.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign exchange receipts, including all wire payments for the sale of food products, subfranchise licensing fees and supply chain goods, must be repatriated to a domestic SAFE-registered bank account in China within 180 days of the date of shipment or service completion, unless the bank grants an extension under SAFE Circular 28/2020. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds under the post-2012 SAFE reform; exporters may retain foreign currency in a settlement account or convert to RMB at their discretion, but the account position must be reported to SAFE on the normal monitoring platform and any retention exceeding the bank's open position limit requires justification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China (China mainland branch network)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Renminbi Capital Account for FDI verification
Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB and Foreign Currency)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB and Foreign Currency)
Foreign Currency Settlement Account for Export Proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low: Offshore digital EMI platforms are not legally permitted to open domestic hold accounts or provide onshore settlement services for a Chinese mainland WFOE without a licensed banking partnership and SAFE cross-border payment qualification. Fintech EMIs may only serve as technical conduits to tier-1 Chinese banks for data transmission and remittance instruction formatting, but they cannot replace a domestically licensed bank for FX settlement, capital verification, or clearing with China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS). Any use of a non-bank EMI for direct USD/RMB conversion or outbound repatriation is barred by the PBOC Non-Bank Payment Institution rules; therefore the WFOE must anchor all clearing onto a licensed onshore bank with a designated SAFE code.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative and at least one board-authorized officer must attend an in-branch KYC interview at the designated tier-1 commercial bank in the city of registration. Remote consular proxy opening is not permissible for a new WFOE with a foreign shareholder; however, the bank may allow the foreign corporate shareholder's authorized signatory to appear via a notarized power-of-attorney only for document submission, not for the final compliance interview, which requires physical presence of the onshore legal representative or a senior onshore manager holding a valid Chinese residence permit and employment proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) chain for the overseas parent entity, especially if the parent jurisdiction is a low-corporate-tax or opaque registry jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, full UBO registry extract or notarized declaration disclosing all individuals holding 25% or more ownership, a bank reference letter from the parent's home bank indicating transaction history a minimum of 12 months, and a corporate organizational chart certified by a licensed CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic or industry linkage mismatched against the WFOE's declared fast-casual food franchise scope, such as unexplained payments to third-party shell suppliers or receipts from non-restaurant code remitters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed and stamped master franchise agreements, licensing contracts, supplier due diligence questionnaires, invoices and bill of lading for each material cross-border transaction, the CATIS (China International Trade Single Window) declaration records, and a written business explanation for any remitter classified outside the ISIC 5610 code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anti-money laundering concern over royalty wire frequency and destination countries presenting inordinate sanctions or exchange-control red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete register of all current and forecast royalty payments, the IP license agreement filed with the National Copyright Administration or local intellectual property office, verified tax payment completion certificates under withholding and VAT regulations, and a legal opinion from the receiving jurisdiction confirming the payee is the tax-beneficial owner under the relevant Double Tax Agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Excessive mismatch between declared paid-in capital and projected operational cash burn for the malatang franchise, which could indicate disguised cross-border lending or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 18-month cash flow projection, lease contracts for planned physical store locations, import/export customs projections for self-serve equipment and broth ingredients, a capital verification report issued by a licensed Chinese CPA firm after the first capital injection, and a certified funds source statement for the foreign shareholder's contribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment capital must be wired through SWIFT MT103 or CNAPS to the WFOE's foreign currency capital account at the designated SAFE bank, with remittance instructions clearly citing the SAFE FDI verification code and purpose code 'Investment in operating enterprise (foreign direct investment)' per the PBOC/SAFE classification. The remitter must be the registered foreign shareholder and the payment reference must include the WFOE's unified social credit code and the SAFE FDI registration number. After funds arrive, the bank will assist in completing the capital registration and the RMB conversion, then transfer proceeds to the Renminbi Capital Account for capital verification. The WFOE must retain the incoming payment advice, SAFE Capital Account Confirmation, CPA capital verification certificate, and strictly use the funds only for purposes within the registered business scope and the approved capital-use schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements should be routed through SWIFT MT103 cash transfers for royalty and service payments, with Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) or Documentary Collections (MT400/MT420) used for the export of packaged broth, sauces, and self-serve equipment to overseas franchisees. All outbound remittances require an approved SAFE payment purpose code: 'Intangible royalties and license fees' for franchise licensing revenues, 'Trade settlement' for goods import/export, and 'Services rendered abroad' for consulting and support services. The clearing must pass through the CIPS rails for RMB cross-border settlements or through SWIFT for USD and other foreign currencies, with the bank acting as the direct clearing member. The WFOE must file accurate transaction justification in the bank's digital FX monitoring portal and retain the underlying contracts, commercial invoices, customs declarations, MOFCOM trade registration, and tax withholding certificates to ensure seamless settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: SAFE-approved onshore foreign exchange forward contracts for hedging receivables and payables under genuine current account trade transactions, with 12-month maturity caps and bank counterparty limit.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only through banks designated by SAFE for offshore renminbi exposures, provided the underlying exposure is documented with a real commercial transaction; onshore direct NDF trading remains restricted.
Currency swaps limited to actual underlying trade or loan exposures with licensed domestic banks under the PBOC derivative framework; speculative swaps without exposure are prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 30 June for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations immediately after the deadline; removal only after formal rectification application. If unfiled for three consecutive years, inclusion in the Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List and administrative strike-off (revocation of business license).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the integrated Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 30 June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Regulatory admonition, credit record impairment, inability to obtain foreign exchange and finance-related approvals; non-filing for three consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return (Annual CIT Reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the Electronic Tax Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the fiscal year immediately following the tax year; quarterly provisional returns due within 15 days after each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; overdue tax accrues daily surcharge of 0.05% of the amount in arrears; wilful non-filing triggers an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and compulsory recovery measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Exchange Business Verification (Foreign-Invested Enterprise)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual verification due by 30 June following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Restriction or suspension of foreign exchange purchase and remittance services; inclusion in negative credit files; SAFE administrative fine for deliberate misreporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Statement Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Enterprise shareholders and Board of Directors; submitted to tax authorities and SAFE upon request; retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed within 120 days of fiscal year-end (by 30 April in practice) to support the annual tax settlement and annual reports; final approval at the annual shareholders' meeting no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the WFOE-specific audit duty may result in administrative action by SAMR, MOFCOM, or SAFE; failure to produce audited statements can lead to a fine under the PRC Accounting Law and inclusion of the enterprise in the credit deficiency list, impacting eventual strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All WFOEs must be audited annually by a PRC-certified public accounting firm, regardless of balance-sheet size, turnover, or employee headcount; there are no quantitative exemptions for foreign-invested enterprises. No asset, revenue, or staff thresholds are prescribed; the audit obligation is unconditional and arises from the enterprise's status as a foreign-invested limited liability company under the PRC Foreign Investment Law and its implementing regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / CAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance, substantially converged with IFRS; small-enterprise accounting standards may be chosen only if the WFOE meets the statutory small-enterprise test, but the standard practice for WFOEs is full CAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any equity transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to SAMR within 30 days of the occurrence, under the PRC Company Law (2023) and the PBOC/SAMR Beneficial Ownership Information Management Measures (effective 1 November 2024). The annual enterprise report filed each year by 30 June serves as the statutory annual confirmation of the enterprise's beneficial ownership data; failure to update in time triggers administrative penalties and credit deterioration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Managers
Corporate Minute Book (shareholder resolutions, board resolutions, supervisor resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,000 - 15,000 per annum (typical registered office lease or agent fee in tier-1 to tier-2 Chinese cities)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 12,000 per annum (depending on transaction volume, payroll, and audit complexity)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China's standard Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rate is 25%. The Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) may qualify for the Small Low-Profit Enterprise (SLPE) preferential regime if annual taxable income does not exceed RMB 3 million, total employees do not exceed 300, and total assets do not exceed RMB 50 million; for SLPE, taxable income is calculated at 25% inclusion and taxed at the 20% reduced rate, producing an effective CIT rate of 5% for the 2023-2027 policy window. No general tax holiday applies to a Malatang franchise licensing and fast-casual restaurant business, and no patent box regime is available for trademark or royalty income unless a separately qualifying government-recognised R&D intangible asset is licensed; such a determination would require rigorous technical appraisal and IP registration, which is not presumed for ordinary franchise branding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000, A Class) together with the mandatory related-party transaction schedules, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration's e-Tax Bureau portal with the WFOE's tax registration identification and digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional CIT prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year WFOE the deadline is May 31 of the following year. Quarterly provisional returns and payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter, specifically by April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 following the fourth quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from restaurant franchise licensing, initial franchise fees, royalty fees, self-serve Ma La Tang bowl sales if company-operated, equipment resale, and other business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross revenue in full without netting out non-resident withholding taxes or DTA-reduced taxes. Any related-party franchise or intercompany service revenue must be booked at arm's length and reconciled to signed contracts and the related-party transaction disclosure schedules; understating revenue attributed to non-resident licensing structures is a red flag for tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs directly attributable to revenue generation, including raw food ingredients, one-time franchise support materials, store equipment cost of sales, staff costs for company-owned stores, and direct operational overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases from a non-resident affiliate must be substantiated with purchase orders, customs/import documentation, freight evidence, and an economic substance explanation of the foreign affiliate's value-added function. If the foreign seller is a shell or lacks storage, logistics, or risk-bearing functions, tax authorities can disallow the cost and recharacterise the transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / A100000 Line 3 - Taxes and Surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business taxes and surcharges excluding CIT and VAT, including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, resource tax, real estate taxes, stamp duty, and related surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident income tax entry is made in this line. Foreign income taxes paid by the WFOE on cross-border income may be claimed through the foreign tax credit mechanism in the later tax computation, not as a deduction in this line. Chinese VAT itself is excluded, but non-creditable VAT on unrelated employee consumption or luxury assets may be capitalised and amortised according to standard rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Franchise marketing campaigns, digital platform channel fees, store promotion materials, brand advertising, franchise recruitment travel, and business development expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Marketing fees paid to a non-resident parent or affiliate are deductible only if the payer receives a concrete and identifiable benefit and the fee reflects a fee for real, substantive services. A bare payment labelled 'global marketing contribution' to a zero-employee offshore entity is typical treaty-shopping and transfer-pricing audit bait; such charges must be backdated, evidenced, benchmarked, and aligned with CIGA in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent, utilities, salaried local management, legal and accounting fees, insurance, franchise training administration, and general office expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees charged by a non-resident shareholder are subject to strict deduction limitation under Chinese tax law: services must be actually rendered, the fee must be arm's length, and the recipient must file an invoice supporting the service. If the non-resident service provider has no employees, no office, no decision-making capacity and simply passes invoices, the entire expense is typically disallowed and penalties imposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on bank loans, intercompany loans, exchange losses, and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest payable to a non-resident lender is subject to 10% CIT withholding unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Treaty, and also to VAT on domestic financial services with a 6% rate if the lender carries on business in China. The thin capitalization rule under the Enterprise Income Tax Law limits deductions: ordinary corporate related-party debt-to-equity ratio is 2:1 and financial institutions 5:1; excess interest is non-deductible and is treated as a dividend distribution for tax purposes. Any back-to-back loan through a Hong Kong conduit with no real treasury function is scrutinised heavily.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / A100000 Line 7 - Asset Impairment and Fair Value Changes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Asset impairment provisions, loss allowances, inventory valuation adjustments, changes in fair value of financial instruments, and investment gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Impairment provisions must be supported by objective evidence and tax adjustment schedules. For cross-border royalty-bearing intangible assets, artificial write-downs or valuations to shift profits abroad must be disclosed in the transfer-pricing schedules; tax authorities may challenge any impairment that is not economically substantive. Non-resident related-party equity holders cannot use a Chinese impairment loss to offset foreign source income without arm's-length valuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating profit calculated as operating revenue minus operating cost, taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, financial expenses, and adjusted impairment and fair value items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that all intercompany adjustments, payments in transit, and treaty protection claims are fully documented before computing operating profit. If the WFOE is consistently loss-making while paying high royalties to an offshore parent, the tax authority will treat this as indicating non-arm's-length pricing and may impute profit under special tax investigation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-tax accounting profit after adding non-operating income and deducting non-operating expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Special attention is paid to abandonment of franchise assets, compensation received from non-resident franchisees, and extrajudicial settlement of IP disputes; these items are generally fully taxable. A non-resident shareholder's forgiveness of intercompany debt is treated as capital contribution or taxable income depending on the facts, and must be disclosed in the tax adjustment schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / A100000 Line 15 - Taxable Income After Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after additions for disallowed expenses, non-deductible provisions, excessive related-party interest, entertainment expense limits, advertising limits, and other statutory add-backs, and after deductions for tax-exempt income and allowable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All non-deductible cross-border expenses, including excessive royalties, management fees lacking substance, and TP adjustments, must be added back line by line in Schedule A105000 and related schedules. The WFOE must file contemporaneous local file and master file where thresholds are met; failure to produce such documentation exposes the taxpayer to a forced adjustment with interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 / A100000 Line 16-17 - Applicable Tax Rate and CIT Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of 25% statutory CIT rate, or the 20% reduced rate with 25% inclusion for a qualifying SLPE WFOE, to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on this resident return; instead, Chinese tax on dividend repatriation is collected separately by withholding at the time of distribution. If treaty relief to 5% is planned, the parent's TRC and beneficial ownership statement must be obtained before dividend distribution; otherwise, full 10% withholding must be reported and paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 / A100000 Line 19 - Final CIT Payable, Credits and Refunds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT payable after non-refundable tax credits, foreign tax credits, and quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits for withholding taxes suffered abroad on non-resident source income are capped at the Chinese CIT attributable to that income. Cross-border dividend withholding paid by the non-resident shareholder is not creditable against the WFOE's CIT liability. If the WFOE uses a fraudulent foreign tax credit arrangement to offset Chinese tax, severe criminal tax evasion penalties apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule A100000-related associated enterprise declaration and the detailed China Related-Party Transactions Summary Table, requiring identification of all related parties, transaction types, pricing policies, and amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every cross-border royalty, loan, service fee, purchase from the non-resident franchisor, and sale of franchise rights must be itemised. The form requires annual related-party transaction totals: services exceeding RMB 40 million, tangible asset transfers exceeding RMB 200 million, and intangible or financial asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million trigger mandatory contemporaneous documentation. Concealing a related party or understating a transaction amount is an administrative violation with automatic interest and penalty exposure and can elevate the file to a criminal tax referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is punished under Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL) Article 62 with a fine of up to RMB 2,000, or between RMB 2,000 and RMB 10,000 for serious cases. Underpayment of CIT due to false filing attracts a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax (TCAL Article 32) and an administrative fine of 50% to five times the underpaid tax (TCAL Article 63). If fraudulent filing results in tax evasion exceeding RMB 100,000 and exceeding 10% of the assessable tax, criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 arises, carrying imprisonment up to three years and a fine; where the evaded amount is huge and exceeds 30%, the director or person in charge faces three to seven years' imprisonment and a fine. Taxpayers listed as dishonest are blacklisted under the Memorandum on Joint Penalties for Dishonest Taxpayers and may be blocked from cross-border travel and government procurement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before a WFOE declares a dividend to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, the withholding agent must determine the applicable rate. The statutory withholding rate is 10% under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 27 and Article 37. To claim a treaty reduction, the non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner and provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its jurisdiction of residence, a beneficial ownership declaration substantiating that the shareholder is not a conduit or agent receiving dividends on behalf of a third party, a certificate of incorporation and shareholding records proving the minimum shareholding period, and if applying for the 5% treaty rate, evidence of direct holding of at least 25% of the capital throughout the required 365-day continuous holding period. The withholding agent must file the withholding tax return and apply for DTA relief at the Chinese tax authority before or at distribution; where full 10% has been withheld, the foreign shareholder may apply for a refund within three years under TCAL Article 51. The TRC must cover the year of the dividend income and be authenticated as required by the relevant bilateral treaty; incomplete beneficial ownership documentation results in denial of treaty relief, additional interest, and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate for cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10% under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. In addition, cross-border payments for royalties and certain financing services may be subject to Chinese Value-Added Tax at 6% unless zero-rated; the VAT is generally borne by the payer and may be non-creditable for the non-resident. Under most Chinese Double Tax Treaties, interest and royalties may be reduced to 10%, 7%, 5%, or in limited cases 0%, depending on the treaty and the beneficial ownership; for example, treaty relationships commonly reduce dividend withholding to 5% for a 25% corporate shareholder and set royalties at 7-10%. Treaty relief requires submission of the TRC, evidence that the non-resident is beneficial owner, contract terms, and appropriate reporting of the Chinese-source nature of the income. Royalties paid to a non-resident offshore affiliate must also pass the arm's-length and economic substance tests; excessive royalty deductions routinely trigger transfer-pricing audits and irrebuttable business purpose challenges.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File/contemporaneous documentation is mandatory if the annual related-party transaction amount exceeds RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions, RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers, or RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers. Master File preparation is triggered when the aggregate amount of related-party transactions exceeds RMB 1 billion or when the China taxpayer is part of a multinational group with a total group annual consolidated revenue exceeding RMB 5.5 billion and conducting covered transactions in China.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although China does not administer a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime of the type used by zero-tax offshore hubs, the tax authority applies substantive economic analysis under the Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41, 45, and 47, and under the General Anti-Avoidance Rules in TCAL Article 122. A WFOE deriving income from a Malatang franchise licensing business must maintain staff, premises, books and records, contract negotiation, management decisions, accounting functions, and core franchising and menu-development activities inside China. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for a franchise business are treated as occurring where strategic decisions regarding the trademark, brand format, franchisee selection, store standards, supply-chain oversight, and quality assessment are made. If a Hong Kong or other offshore entity is inserted merely to own the trademark and collect royalties while the WFOE performs all value-adding functions in China, the Chinese tax authority can reattribute the profit to China, disregard the offshore entity for tax purposes, impose a deemed taxable presence, and assess interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE under-reports cash and POS revenue from self-serve Ma La Tang stores, suppresses royalty and franchise fees, uses unrelated or false VAT invoices to inflate operating costs, and files a CIT return that conceals taxable income and royalty transactions with the non-resident franchisor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection and Administration Law Articles 32 and 63 require full recovery of the underpaid tax plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and impose a fine of 50% to five times the tax shortage. Criminal Law Article 201 treats evasion of a relatively large tax amount above 10% of assessable tax as criminal tax fraud, punishable by imprisonment up to three years and a fine; evasion is considered huge and above 30% of assessable tax, increasing the penalty to three to seven years' imprisonment and a fine. In addition, the taxpayer is placed on the joint punishment 'dishonest taxpayer' list and faces revocation of business licenses, asset seizures, and cross-border travel restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the director or supervisor authorises false accounts, commingles personal assets with company assets, authorises forged invoices, or causes the company to be unable to pay tax, Chinese courts will pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20 and hold the director jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax and related damages. Tax authorities may impose travel bans and exit controls under TCAL Article 44 against the legal representative and responsible director, and in a serious evasion case the director faces personal criminal prosecution, monetary fines, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Stripping Through a Shell Conduit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE makes excessive royalty, trademark licence, and management fee payments to a non-resident affiliate located in a low-tax or zero-tax jurisdiction that has no office, no employees, no operational risk, no decision-making functions, and no real commercial activity, artificially reducing the Chinese taxable profit and repatriating value without arm's-length justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41, 45, and 47 and the Special Tax Adjustments Regulations authorise the tax authority to recharacterise the transaction, disallow the inflated deductions, adjust profit to the arm's-length amount, apply the controlled foreign corporation rules, and impose interest on the adjusted tax. TCAL Article 122 confirms that arrangements without a reasonable commercial purpose are recharacterised according to their economic substance. Where documentary obligations are not met despite the RMB 40 million service or RMB 100/200 million intangible/tangible thresholds, the tax authority may presume taxable income, impose a fine of up to RMB 100,000 for failure to furnish contemporaneous evidence, and apply an additional special tax adjustment interest rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who sign intercompany agreements and approve payments that lack substance can be held personally liable for the shortfall if the asset stripping renders the company insolvent, under the corporate veil-piercing doctrine in Company Law Article 20. The tax bureau can blacklist the responsible legal representative, freeze personal bank accounts where funds were misappropriated, and restrict exit from China under cross-border tax enforcement. If the scheme also involves fraudulent refunds or falsified contracts, the directors face criminal fraud or tax evasion charges with imprisonment up to seven years and restitution of all diverted assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Distribution and Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares and pays dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding the statutory 10% CIT, fails to file the withholding return, or relies on a treaty without providing a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership substantiation, resulting in unpaid Chinese tax on outbound profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 37 and Article 40 impose withholding obligations on the WFOE as payer. Under TCAL Article 69, a withholding agent that fails to withhold or fails to pay over withheld tax is subject to administrative recovery, a daily surcharge on unpaid tax, and a fine of 50% to three times the tax that should have been withheld and paid. The non-resident shareholder remains liable for the tax, and the WFOE cannot deduct the dividend WHT as a corporate expense. Illegal distributions made while the company has no distributable profits are void and subject to Company Law penalties and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who declare and approve an illegal dividend without required reserves, loss offsets, or tax withholding can be ordered by the court to repay the distributed funds to the company and are liable for damages to creditors under Company Law Article 152 and Article 166. In the cross-border context, the legal representative may be listed as a dishonest violator, subjected to exit denial and visa suspension, and, when the company is liquidated without settling withholding liabilities, can be prosecuted under Criminal Law for refusal to pay tax or for false liquidation, leading to imprisonment and personal criminal fines.
